title: Board Grammar Mastery (CBSE/ISC)
description: Final board grammar mastery for Grade 12 (CBSE/ISC): advanced gap filling, editing with style and collocation errors, and complex rewriting — full exam practice with bilingual notes and tests.

topics.title: Advanced Gap Filling & Editing
topics.concept:
Advanced gap filling goes beyond simple tenses to test:

  • Verb forms in formal/literary contexts (perfect, passive, subjunctive).
  • Complex modals and modal perfects (must have, would have).
  • Determiners and articles with abstract nouns.
  • Prepositions in formal collocations.

Always read the whole passage; let the surrounding grammar fix each gap.

Advanced editing at board level includes three error layers:

  • Grammatical: tense, agreement, articles, prepositions.
  • Collocation: wrong word partnerships — do a mistake → make a mistake; strong rain → heavy rain; say a lie → tell a lie.
  • Style: redundancy, wrong register, awkward phrasing — more better → better; revert back → revert.

examples.problem: Edit (collocation): She did a big mistake in the exam.
examples.solution: did → made: 'She made a big mistake in the exam.'

examples.problem: Gap fill (modal perfect): The ground is wet; it ___ rained last night.
examples.solution: must have rained — a confident deduction about the past.

recap: Gap filling: verb forms, modals, articles in formal/literary text
Editing has three layers: grammar, collocation, style
Collocation errors: do a mistake → make; strong rain → heavy

topics.title: Complex Rewriting & Full Practice
topics.concept:
Complex rewriting bundles together every transformation skill. Typical board directions:

  • Change the voice (all tenses, special cases).
  • Change the narration (mixed passages, precise reporting verbs).
  • Combine into one sentence (synthesis: participle, infinitive, relative, apposition).
  • Rewrite as directed: 'Begin with…', 'Use the given word', 'Change the degree'.
  • Conditional and inversion transforms (Had I…, No sooner…).

Exam strategy:

  1. Read the instruction twice — the marks are for following it exactly.
  2. Identify the grammar point being tested.
  3. Keep the meaning unchanged.
  4. Check tense, agreement and word forms before moving on.

With these reflexes automatic, the grammar section becomes a source of guaranteed marks.

examples.problem: Rewrite beginning with 'Hardly': As soon as the bell rang, the class ended.
examples.solution: Hardly had the bell rung when the class ended.

examples.problem: Change the voice: The principal will award the prizes.
examples.solution: The prizes will be awarded by the principal.

recap: Rewriting bundles voice, narration, synthesis and transformation
Follow the exact direction; keep the meaning
Check tense, agreement and word forms before finalising

questions.q: Correct: 'He did a mistake.'
Correct: 'There was strong rain.'
Gap: 'By 9, the show ___ already started.'
Voice: 'They are repairing the road.'
Begin with 'Hardly': 'As soon as he spoke, the crowd cheered.'
options: Hardly he had spoken when the crowd cheered.
Hardly had he spoken when the crowd cheered.
Hardly did he spoke than the crowd cheered.
Hardly spoke he when the crowd cheered.

questions.q: Correct: 'She said a lie.'
Gap (modal perfect): 'He ___ missed the bus; he's late.'
Narration: 'He said, "I will help."'
options: He said that he would help.
He said that I would help.

questions.q: Correct: 'It is more better.'
Voice: 'Someone has stolen my pen.'
Gap (subjunctive): 'It is vital that he ___ present.'
Correct: 'We discussed about it.'
Edit the line (give all corrections): 'Neither of the plans were accept by the committee.'
questions.explanation: 'Neither' is singular → 'was'; and the passive needs 'accepted'.

questions.q: Rewrite beginning with 'Not until': 'He understood the danger only when it was too late.'
options: Not until it was too late did he understand the danger.
Not until it was too late he understood the danger.
Not until did it was too late he understood.
Not until too late was it he understood.

questions.q: Identify the collocation error: 'The scientist did a remarkable discovery.'
Change the voice with a reporting verb: 'People believe that he has resigned.'
options: He is believed to have resigned.
It is believe that he resigned.

questions.q: Combine into one sentence (synthesis): 'The storm subsided. The rescue began. It saved many lives.'
options: The storm having subsided, the rescue began and saved many lives.
The storm subsided the rescue began saving lives.
Subsiding the storm, the rescue saved lives began.
The rescue began the storm subsided saving lives.
questions.explanation: Absolute phrase + coordinated verbs combine the three ideas.

questions.q: Gap fill (formal/literary): 'Little ___ he know that fortune awaited him.'
Edit for style: 'In my personal opinion, I think the plan is good.'
options: Remove 'personal' and 'I think' (redundant): 'In my opinion, the plan is good.'
questions.explanation: 'personal opinion' and 'I think' are redundant together.

questions.q: Rewrite as directed (degree): 'Very few writers are as influential as Shakespeare.'
options: Shakespeare is one of the most influential writers.
Shakespeare is more influential than writers.
Shakespeare is as influential as writers.
questions.explanation: 'Very few … as … as' → 'one of the most …'.

outcomes: Edit for grammatical, style and collocation errors
Rewrite and combine complex sentences accurately
Apply every grammar rule under exam conditions
Use a clear, accurate answer format

intro.en: This is the capstone: a full, exam-focused workout that pulls together everything from Grades 6–12. CBSE and ISC papers test grammar through three demanding tasks — advanced gap filling, editing (now including style and collocation errors), and complex rewriting. Master these under timed conditions and the grammar section of your board exam is secure.
intro.hi: यह शिखर है: एक पूर्ण, परीक्षा-केंद्रित अभ्यास जो कक्षा 6–12 की हर बात को समेटता है। CBSE और ISC पेपर तीन कठिन कार्यों से व्याकरण जाँचते हैं — advanced gap filling, editing (अब style और collocation त्रुटियों सहित), और complex rewriting। इन्हें समयबद्ध परिस्थितियों में साध लें तो आपके बोर्ड पेपर का व्याकरण-खंड सुरक्षित।

real_life.situation:
A subtle editing line (style + collocation):

Line: The committee made a strong effort to do a decision quickly.
Fix: made a strong effort → made every effort; do a decision → make a decision.
real_life.why: At this level, editing isn't only about obvious grammar — it tests collocation ('make a decision') and style ('made every effort'). Spotting these refined errors is what separates a top score from an average one.

items.q: By the time help arrived, the fire ______ (spread) everywhere.
It is essential that every candidate ______ (be) punctual.
The decision ______ (take) yesterday was unpopular. (passive participle)

error_detection.sentence: He gave a strong effort to win.
error_detection.correct: He made every effort to win.

error_detection.sentence: The reason is because he was absent.
error_detection.correct: The reason is that he was absent.

sentence_correction.wrong: Change the voice: 'They are constructing a new road.'
sentence_correction.correct: A new road is being constructed (by them).

sentence_correction.wrong: Begin with 'No sooner': 'As soon as he arrived, it rained.'
sentence_correction.correct: No sooner had he arrived than it rained.

sentence_correction.wrong: Combine: 'She was tired. She finished the race.'
sentence_correction.correct: Though tired, she finished the race. (or: Tired, she finished the race.)

rearrangement.jumbled: had / the / rung / no / sooner / bell / than / left / we
rearrangement.answer: No sooner had the bell rung than we left.

rearrangement.jumbled: being / road / a / constructed / new / is
rearrangement.answer: A new road is being constructed.

reading.passage:
Board editing passage (one error per line, corrections shown):

L1: The principal made a important announcement. (a → an)
L2: He said that the school will remain closed. (will → would)
L3: Students were ask to stay at home. (ask → asked)
L4: Many of them did a sigh of relief. (did → heaved/gave)
L5: Hardly the news had spread when phones began ringing. (Hardly the news had → Hardly had the news)

questions.q: What kind of error is on Line 2?
questions.answer: A sequence-of-tenses / reported-speech error — after a past reporting verb, 'will' becomes 'would'.

questions.q: Identify the collocation error and its fix.
questions.answer: Line 4: 'did a sigh' → 'heaved/gave a sigh' (correct collocation).

questions.q: What rule does Line 5 test?
questions.answer: Inversion after 'Hardly': 'Hardly had the news spread when…'.

speaking: There was heavy rain all night.
No sooner had we left than it rained.
The work will be completed soon.

writing.prompt: Write a 5-line passage with one error per line (mixing grammar, collocation and style errors), then give the corrections — a full board-style editing exercise.
writing.example: Line: He did a great effort. (did → made)

micro_quiz.q: Begin with 'No sooner': 'As soon as I slept, the alarm rang.'
options: No sooner had I slept than…
No sooner did I slept than…

challenge.q: Edit (two errors): 'The childrens was ask to leave.'
options: childrens → children; was ask → were asked

challenge.q: Rewrite using 'Scarcely': 'The train had just left when we reached.'
options: Scarcely had the train left when we reached.
Scarcely the train had left when we reached.
Scarcely did the train leave than we reached.
Scarcely left the train when we reached.

challenge.q: Change the voice (reporting verb): 'People expect him to win.'
options: It is expect that he wins.
